column2: Early Sunday at the Sant Antoni flea market. Yuna and Marc, a reserved locksmith of few words, look for the son of the old photographer of "Foto Avenida" among a hundred stalls. They ask around; a stamp seller points them to Quique, who sells photos of strangers. Hopeful, searching.
a little worried, looking at all the stalls
dry and brief: "many", and the answer is "by asking"
brief and matter-of-fact, pointing the way

At Quique's corner stall, full of shoe boxes of old photos. Quique, a calm man in his seventies, explains that his father kept every uncollected photo in envelopes, sure someone would return one day. He brings out the Tibidabo box; Yuna and Marc search the 1978 envelopes until Marc stops at one. Slow, tense, held breath.
slow and kind, a little sad at "Nunca volvió nadie"

Yuna opens the envelope: a small black-and-white photo of young Martí looking at her grandmother, her mother at three, laughing, and her grandmother at twenty-seven with a big smile Yuna never saw on her face. Marc sees his grandfather young for the first time. Quique refuses payment: it was paid in 1978. Deeply moved, very quiet.

column1: Es mi abuelo. Nunca lo he visto
Y es mi abuela. Y mi madre.

column2: kind, raising a hand to refuse the money

On a bench by the market, Marc reads the envelope label aloud and says the photographer thought the three were a family. The thought stays with Yuna like a stone in a shoe. They send the photo to Yuna's mother in Korea, who asks who the man is; Yuna cannot answer. Quiet and unsettled.
carefully, a thought he isn't sure he should say
